# Ratte (01, engineer) — BAD-080

## Brief
Close the gap BAD-063's server-side grace was built to stand behind: a take that is still being delivered must keep its own seat hot, so the grace covers only another member's poll landing mid-upload, never the pushing client's own reads.

## The defect

A collab room wraps on a read when no seat has a fresh `recording_at`. Both shipped clients null their own `recording_at` at the stop beat (`collabHeartbeat(false)` / `collab:heartbeat` with `recording: false`) and then open the push with an `info` call — a read. That read is what completes the wrap, under the pusher's own delivery, before `upload-url` is ever attempted. BAD-063 made the server admit such a take for `WRAP_GRACE_MS` after `wrapped_at`; the comment at `server/supabase/functions/_shared/collab.mjs:112-127` says in as many words that this is the case standing aside cannot cover. The design's intent is that whoever is mid-part finishes, and the client is the only party that knows a take is still in flight.

## What to build

The client-side fix, on both shipped clients. Pick whichever of these two shapes the code actually supports best, and say in your Result which you chose and why:

- **Keep the seat hot until the commit lands** — hold `recording: true` on the heartbeat from the stop beat through the last `commit` of the push, so the seat never goes cold underneath a delivery in progress; or
- **Stop opening a push with an `info` round trip**, so the pushing client is not itself the read that completes the wrap.

Either way the invariant to land is: *a client that is mid-delivery never causes, and is never caught by, its own wrap.* Whichever you choose, the server's `WRAP_GRACE_MS` must end up as the belt for another member's poll, not the path the pusher normally takes.

A server-side hot window (a `recording_stopped_at` / `hot_until` column on `collab_claims`) is the explicitly named alternative and is **out of scope** — it needs a migration, and no migration is in your deliverables. If your investigation concludes the client fix cannot hold the invariant without one, `member block` with the evidence rather than writing SQL.

Note the honesty constraint the server module states at `collab.mjs:91-95` and `:306-311`: a heartbeat that reads as recording holds the wrap open and shows other members "@x is recording". If you keep the seat hot through the push, make sure what the other members are told stays true — "delivering a take" is not the same claim as "at the mic". Read those comments before you choose, and if your fix would make the strip lie, say so and choose the other shape.

## The two clients

- **Web** (`web/`, which the iOS shell inherits unmodified): `web/collabweb-sync.js` — `pushTakes()` at :8-52 opens with `collabFetch('info', …)` then `upload-url` → PUT → `commit`; `collabHeartbeat(recording)` at :173-186 and `startBoothHeartbeat()` at :187-193 (60s idle tick). `web/booth.js:348` beats `true` on record start, `:373` beats `false` on stop. `runCollabSync` at `collabweb-sync.js:101` is the caller.
- **Desktop**: `main.js` `collab:push` at :4006 (same info-then-upload shape) and `collab:heartbeat` at :4240-4248; the renderer owns the cadence at `renderer/app.js:6183` (`window.vc.collabHeartbeat`) and pushes at `:5932` (`window.vc.collabPush`); the bridge is `preload.js:153`.

Keep the two clients' behaviour the same — this is one rule living in two places, and they must agree. If a piece of it belongs in a shared module rather than written twice, propose it (`proposal file`) rather than restructuring here.

## Ticket proposals
- **Move the collab delivery rule into src/collab.js instead of writing it twice** — suggested P2; created as [[BAD-089]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: BAD-080 lands one rule — 'a take's delivery makes no read' — in two clients that cannot share code from my deliverables. collabTakeInFlight() and collabIdleBeat() are now near-identical in web/collabweb-sync.js and renderer/app.js, and the set of modes that ARE a delivery (upload-url, commit) is stated in collab/room.ts, implied in both clients and re-derived by regex in test/collabdelivery.test.js. src/collab.js is already the UMD module both processes load for exactly this reason ('one file is what keeps those two answers from drifting'), so a DELIVERY_MODES export plus a pure takeInFlight({pushInFlight, debounce, queued}) predicate would make it one definition with one unit test, instead of two copies pinned by a source-text assertion.
  Evidence: web/collabweb-sync.js and renderer/app.js each declare collabPushInFlight + collabTakeInFlight + collabIdleBeat with the same three terms; test/collabdelivery.test.js's 'both clients hold the booth tick on the same three terms' exists only because there is no shared definition to test once. src/collab.js already exports claimFresh, claimRecording, CLAIM_LEASE_MS and RECORDING_FRESH_MS to both. src/collab.js was outside BAD-080's deliverables.
- **One info read per collab sync, not two — fold pullTakes onto the same snapshot** — suggested P2; created as [[BAD-090]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: After BAD-080 the sync loop still takes two 'info' reads per cycle on both clients: pullTakes() opens with one of its own, and refreshCollab takes the trailing one. Each is a read, and a read is what completes a wrapping room's wrap. The pull's read is safe today only because runCollabSync awaits the push before it (nothing is in flight when it fires), which is an ordering nobody has written down. Folding pullTakes onto the snapshot the way pushTakes now does would halve collab polling traffic for every member, remove one more wrap-completing read from the client's own loop, and make the ordering an invariant rather than a coincidence.
  Evidence: web/collabweb-sync.js pullTakes():59 and main.js collab:pull both do collabFetch('info') before their download loop; runCollabSync then calls refreshCollab, which fetches info again. With 8 members at a 60s poll that is 16 info reads a minute for a room instead of 8. BAD-080 deliberately left pullTakes alone: it was not in the ticket's 'what to build', and a pull is not a delivery.

## Result
Chose shape B — the delivery makes no read — on both clients; shape A (hold recording:true through the push) would have made the strip lie, because claimRecording drives a live 'rec' waveLoader and the literal sentence '@x is recording' (renderer/app.js:4594, :5289-5325; web/collabweb-phases.js:243-251), and renderer:5321 already comments 'the loader only while truly live' (D2, 'never a frozen recording…').

Built, uncommitted on fix/bad-080-hot-seat: (1) the push no longer opens with info — web pushTakes() decides from collab.info, main collab:push from collabInfoSnaps, each falling back to one look only when there is NO snapshot (a room the client has never seen, which cannot be mid-part); the wrap is then decided inside commit, after the row lands, which wraps the room over the take. (2) The booth's IDLE heartbeat is held while a take is owed — collabIdleBeat + collabTakeInFlight (push armed on the debounce, queued, or bytes moving) in both clients; only the COLD beat is held, since completeWrap probes the seat before the handler restamps it, so a hot beat and the two edge beats at record start/stop cannot complete a wrap and still go immediately. (3) main's 60s info poller stands aside for a room in collabDelivering. Server untouched; WRAP_GRACE_MS now covers only another member's poll landing mid-upload.

Files: main.js, renderer/app.js, preload.js, web/collabweb-sync.js, web/booth.js, web/CLAUDE.md, renderer/CLAUDE.md, and new test/collabdelivery.test.js.

Verified: npm test 1825/1703 pass/0 fail/122 skip (pack tests RAN, 23 voicepacks linked; skips are the server-integration suite with functions not served, plus the mobile build test). SMOKE_SCOPE=booth npm run smoke -> SMOKE_OK, exit 0, screenshots inspected. The new suite is a proven pin, not a spelling check: restoring HEAD's web/collabweb-sync.js failed 7 of its 11 tests, restoring the fix passed all 11; it drives the real web sync in a vm against a recorded wire and reads the stand-aside modes out of collab/room.ts rather than retyping them. Desktop halves are structure-pinned (Electron, no unit harness) plus the smoke run.

Left: deciding against a snapshot means a seat claimed in the last instant may not be in it, so a first take saved inside that round trip goes out with the next push instead of immediately — stated in both files' comments with why the obvious guard is not there (a host owns characterless lines with no claim row, so 'look when I hold no claim' would put the read back on the path for hosts). Proposals 123 (move the rule into src/collab.js — it is written twice and pinned by regex) and 124 (one info read per sync: fold pullTakes onto the snapshot too).

## Outcome
Chose the shape that keeps the booth strip honest: the delivery makes no read, rather than a heartbeat claiming the mic while bytes upload. Backed the change with a pin that fails against the old sync.
